column1: # cheatah-space CDF differential corpus — the pinned, hash-verified reference files.
# Columns (tab-separated):  tier  file  url  sha256  bytes  tags
# WHAT THIS IS. The files space.cdf is verified against, byte for byte, using NASA's own library
# as the oracle. Every row was fetched and hashed on 2026-08-28; every tag was DERIVED from the
# file by `scripts/cdf-corpus.sh probe` (which reads it with cdfdump), not typed by hand. Re-run
# probe after adding a row — a hand-written tag is a claim, a derived one is a measurement.
# The files themselves are NEVER committed. They live in the .gitignore'd
# space/cdf/vendor/corpus/ and are fetched on demand. This manifest is the committed part: it is
# what makes the corpus reproducible and what makes "the file changed upstream" detectable.
# TIERS
#   tier0  ~3.0 MB   unit fixtures. Always fetched. Small enough to run in seconds.
#   tier1  ~68 MB    real mission data. The correctness sweep.
#   tier2  ~470 MB   large files, benchmarks only. Never in the default oracle ctest.
# THE GAP THIS CORPUS CANNOT CLOSE. Not one file in NASA's public archive uses RLE, Huffman,
# adaptive Huffman, or whole-file (CCR) compression — verified across all 16 rows below, where
# every compressed variable is GZIP. Those four code paths are therefore covered only by tier3,
# which `scripts/cdf-corpus.sh derive` GENERATES locally with NASA's cdfconvert. Tier3 is not
# listed here: its hashes depend on the oracle build, so it carries its own generated manifest.
# There is likewise no VAX-encoded file anywhere in the archive; see the tier3 notes.
# TAG VOCABULARY
#   v3 | v2.6 | pre-v2.6      on-disk format generation, read from the magic number.
#                             pre-v2.6 is present so the REJECTION path has a real fixture.
#   network | ibmpc | ...     encoding, i.e. the byte order values are stored in.
#   row | column              majority.
#   checksum                  the file carries the trailing 16-byte MD5.
#   var-gzip | var-rle | ...  per-variable compression actually present in the file.
#   ccr-*                     whole-file compression (none exist in the wild; see above).
#   epoch | epoch16 | tt2000  which of the three time types appear.
#   char                      CDF_CHAR/CDF_UCHAR variables or attribute entries.
#   sparse-pad | sparse-prev  sparse record variables, and which fill rule.
#   rvars | zvars             rVariables and/or zVariables present.
#   multifile                 data lives in .v0/.z0 companion files rather than one dotCDF.
